text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Six opposition cadres are sentenced to a suspended prison term for collecting voters cards illegally in a don't-vote campaign.
- Health minister Katele Kalumba bans the sale of a drug that purportedly cures AIDS until it is scientifically cleared.
- A Lusaka court refuses opposition parties challenging the conduct of general elections last year, from examining 38,000 voters cards.
- New South African high commissioner Advocate Tabethe says he will lobby his country's businessmen to invest more in Zambia.
- Corridor disease kills hundreds of cattle in southern Zambia.
- France to provide $320,000 for the construction of a street kids training centre in Lusaka.
